text_span: Portfolio optimization has always been a challenging proposition in finance and management.
rationale: States the central problem motivating the review.

text_span: different classical, statistical and intelligent approaches employed for portfolio optimization and management are reviewed.
rationale: Summarizes the paper’s review scope and method.

code_label: Machine learning and AI support decisions
text_span: recent advances in machine learning and artificial intelligence can help portfolio managers to take right decisions regarding allotment of portfolios.
rationale: Claims practical value of ML/AI for portfolio allocation decisions.

code_label: Comparative study claimed as first of its kind
text_span: A comparative study of different techniques, first of its kind, is presented in this paper.
rationale: Highlights a claimed novelty in comparative synthesis.

text_span: An effort is also made to compile classical, intelligent, and quantum-inspired techniques that can be employed in portfolio optimization.
rationale: Describes inclusion of quantum-inspired methods in the review.

code_label: Transaction costs motivate asset selection limits
text_span: an optimum number of asset selection is important to reduce the transaction cost.
rationale: Identifies transaction cost as a reason for limiting assets.

text_span: a proximal approach involving time penalization is proposed
rationale: Notes a specific method used to handle transaction costs.

text_span: Selection of limited number of assets makes the investment more manageable and explainable
rationale: States an observed benefit of sparse asset selection.

code_label: Regularization needed due to estimation error
text_span: Most of the methods used in portfolio selection proces suffers from estimation error and hence there is a need to regularize the portfolio process
rationale: Explicitly states a limitation in existing methods and need for regularization.

code_label: Reinforcement learning suits dynamic portfolio management
text_span: portfolio management techniques requires a dynamic decision making process and hence a reinforcement based learning techniques are highly suitable to effectively manage the portfolios.
rationale: Argues for RL as suitable for dynamic portfolio decisions.

text_span: Portfolio management requires careful SWOT (Strength-Weakness-Opportunity-Threat) analysis across all the investments.
rationale: Describes a broad analytical requirement for portfolio management.

code_label: Classical methods evolved to advanced heuristics
text_span: portfolio optimization techniques have also evolved from techniques like mean-variance (MV)
rationale: Marks the historical progression from classical to advanced methods.

code_label: Mean-variance minimizes variance at target return
text_span: The objective of the MV model is to find the weight of the assets that will minimize the variance at a given rate of return.
rationale: Defines the core optimization objective of mean-variance.

text_span: The challenge in the MV model arises when it tries to compute covariance and hence cannot be employed in large scale portfolio optimization problems.
rationale: States a scalability limitation of the MV model.

code_label: MAD suited to large diversified problems
text_span: The mean-absolute deviation (MAD) model ... can be employed for large scale and highly diversified portfolio selection problems.
rationale: Identifies the intended use case for MAD.

text_span: The model takes advantages of reduction in computational complexity and provides optimum results.
rationale: Reports a claimed computational and solution-quality benefit.

code_label: MAD penalizes both directions of deviation
text_span: This model suffers a drawback, as it penalizes both positive and negative deviations.
rationale: Explicitly states a drawback of MAD.

code_label: Minimax uses minimum return as risk
text_span: Minimax (MM) ... uses the minimum return as a measure of risk.
rationale: Defines the risk measure used by minimax.

code_label: Minimax is fast via linear programming
text_span: Minimax ... is fast due to its property of linear programming and can be employed for more complex models and constraints.
rationale: States computational advantages of minimax.

text_span: One of the disadvantages of Minimax ... is its sensitivity to outliers, and hence it cannot be employed when the historical data is missing.
rationale: States a limitation and data requirement.

text_span: Lower Partial Moment (LPM) ... uses a set of moments to estimate downside risk in a portfolio.
rationale: Defines the purpose of LPM.

text_span: multiple such kinds of moments.
rationale: Indicates the model can involve multiple moments for analysis.

text_span: While VaR ... is fairly a simplistic technique, it does not consider risk measures.
rationale: States a key limitation of VaR.

text_span: a conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) ... based technique can be employed to consider risk measures.
rationale: Introduces CVaR as a risk-aware alternative.

text_span: CVaR ... can be employed in volatile scenarios and helps in managing risk more efficiently as compared to VaR
rationale: Claims improved risk management under volatility.

text_span: CVaR ... suffers a major disadvantage that it cannot indicate the maximum loss that can be incurred.
rationale: Explicitly states a limitation of CVaR.

code_label: Bayesian networks model risk and return
text_span: Portfolio optimization as proposed in Shenoy and Shenoy (2000) uses a Bayesian network to model risk and return.
rationale: Describes a Bayesian modeling approach for portfolio risk-return.

code_label: Bayesian approach combines qualitative and quantitative data
text_span: it combines historical data with qualitative information to draw a relationship between different portfolios.
rationale: Highlights the data integration feature of the Bayesian approach.

text_span: SVR ... is a machine learning based approach where historical data is fed to the SVR ... to learn the pattern from the historical path.
rationale: Describes the learning mechanism of SVR in this context.

text_span: SVM ... has certain advantages over statistical based techniques like ... effective in high dimensional space
rationale: States a comparative advantage of SVM.

text_span: when the data points are linearly separable, but in the scenario when there is overlap, it underperforms.
rationale: States a performance limitation under non-separable data.

code_label: Neural networks refine learning from history
text_span: The hidden layers help to refine learning from historical data.
rationale: Describes the role of hidden layers in learning.

text_span: uses a performance-based regularization (PBR) function, which helps in reducing the estimation error.
rationale: Reports a benefit of performance-based regularization.

text_span: It has been found that recurrent neural networks (RNN) are very efficient in understanding temporal dependencies.
rationale: States a capability relevant to time-series portfolio data.

text_span: The objective is to maximize the total reward.
rationale: Defines the RL objective in the paper.

text_span: the weight can be dynamically computed against static weights used in traditional approaches.
rationale: Describes dynamic weighting as a key RL feature.

code_label: RL portfolio methods handle changing markets
text_span: can be used to adaptively learn based on changing states.
locator: Table 6 Comparative study of classical and intelligent approaches
rationale: Summarizes the adaptive advantage of RL-based approaches.

text_span: Evolutionary computing ... is a computational intelligence technique inspired from the biological evolution process.
rationale: Defines the conceptual basis of evolutionary methods.

text_span: PSO ... is robust and can be applied for determining non-smooth global optimization problems
rationale: States a key advantage of PSO.

text_span: One of the challenges with PSO is that it lacks mathematical foundation and is difficult to apply in real life scenarios.
rationale: Explicitly states a limitation of PSO.

text_span: ACO ... is a probabilistic model designed to select the best path designed based on pheromone-based communication of biological ants.
rationale: Describes the mechanism of ACO.

code_label: ACO convergence not guaranteed in time
text_span: Time of convergence is not guaranteed.
rationale: States a convergence caveat for ACO.

text_span: multi-objective evolutionary techniques ... have gained popularity in the recent past due to their ability to find multiple pareto-optimal solutions
rationale: Explains why multi-objective methods are useful.

code_label: Quantum computing may solve hard problems
text_span: quantum and quantum-inspired computing techniques can help solve difficult optimization problems
rationale: States the motivation for quantum approaches.

code_label: Qubit as smallest unit of information
text_span: Qubit is the smallest unit of information in quantum computing
rationale: Defines the basic quantum information unit.

text_span: a qubit can be represented as a superposition of two basis states
rationale: Describes the quantum principle underlying quantum-inspired methods.

text_span: have been shown to perform better than the classical counterparts
rationale: States comparative performance of quantum-inspired metaheuristics.

text_span: These algorithms resort to qubit based encoding
rationale: Describes the encoding strategy used by quantum-inspired algorithms.

code_label: Quantum-inspired tabu search improves trading rules
text_span: a quantum-inspired Tabu Search (QTS) ... algorithm is used to find the optimum combination of trading rules
rationale: Describes a specific quantum-inspired optimization application.

code_label: D-Wave and tensor network handle large systems
text_span: the D-Wave hybrid quantum annealing, and tensor network are able to handle large systems of approximately, 1272 fully-connected qubits
rationale: Reports a result from the cited quantum portfolio study, while noting the annealing component.

text_span: QIAEA gives the best performance in terms of precision and recall as compared to the classical GA
rationale: States a comparative performance finding for QIAEA.

code_label: Evolutionary methods stand in good stead
text_span: the evolutionary optimization methods stand in good stead when it comes to optimized allocation of portfolios.
rationale: Summarizes the paper’s overall assessment of evolutionary methods.

text_span: the evolving quantum-inspired evolutionary techniques also promise to be better viable alternatives.
rationale: Indicates promise of quantum-inspired methods as alternatives.

code_label: Better portfolio model remains a challenge
text_span: evolution of a better portfolio model is a challenge for the overall performance improvement of these portfolio optimization techniques.
rationale: States an unresolved challenge and limitation.

code_label: Robust efficient optimization still needs investigation
text_span: robust and efficient optimization techniques remain to be investigated for yielding better optimization scenarios
rationale: Explicitly identifies future research needs.
